insight.title: Why You Feel the Curb Through Your Car Tires
insight.subtitle: Why you feel a physical jolt when you drop your phone.

sections.text: Your brain doesn’t actually know where your skin ends. It is constantly adopting the objects you use — like your car or your phone — as literal, physical extensions of your own body.
When you hold a tool, your mind stops seeing it as an external object. It begins to treat the item like a new limb, mapping its edges as if they were your own flesh.
This is why you wince when a pebble hits your windshield. You aren’t just reacting to a noise; your brain is registering a physical strike against what it now perceives as your body.
Your brain doesn’t know where you end and your tools begin.
